references.text: The creation account describes how God created the animals on the earth and the birds in the sky, the same creatures that Israel was warned against making idols of.
The second commandment forbids making carved images of anything in heaven or on the earth, which directly corresponds to the prohibition against making images of animals and birds.
The immediate context warns Israel against making idols in the form of any creature, including animals on the earth and birds in the sky.
Isaiah mocks idolatry where people make god-images out of wood and worship them, in contrast to the living God.
Paul describes how people exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal humans, birds, four-footed animals, and reptiles.
The psalm reminds us how Israel at Horeb made a calf and worshipped a cast image, exchanging their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass.
